problem:
Compute $P(X>4)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<1, \\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{{x}^{3}}},\, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>4) & =P(4<X<\infty ) \\  & ={\int }_{4}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{4}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}]}_{4}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
